title: kv-cache: defragmentation, paging spillover, and eviction policy improvements
author: Liang Chen
description:
Motivation: We observed two related issues in high-concurrency inference workloads: (1) long-running instances accumulate many small KV cache fragments causing effective usable cache to drop (logical fragmentation), and (2) when memory pressure spikes (heavy batching or long-context requests) the current eviction policy causes expensive full-cache flushes and increased tail latency. This PR introduces three coordinated improvements: a background defragmentation pass, a paging/spillover mechanism to move cold KV segments to an LRU-backed spill store (hot cache remains in GPU/host RAM), and an adaptive eviction policy that prefers compacting or spilling cold segments over aggressive wholesale evictions. Changes are backwards-compatible at the RPC/API layer and gated by feature flags (kv_defrag_enabled, kv_spillover_enabled, kv_adaptive_evict).

What this PR does (summary):
- Add defragmentation worker that coalesces adjacent free fragments in the KV allocator and compacts small segments when low-impact (runtime/kv/allocator.cpp + worker registration).
- Implement a spillover backend that persists cold KV pages to a compressed LRU spill store on host SSD (runtime/kv/spill_store.*). Spill store is configurable per-deployment and disabled by default for on-prem air-gapped installs.
- Introduce an adaptive eviction heuristic that uses per-key access frequency, recent reuse window, and physical fragmentation score to decide: compact-in-place, spill-to-disk, or evict.
- Expose telemetry (metrics and traces) for fragmentation ratio, spill read/write latency, and eviction decisions. Add dashboards and alerts (observability/kv-metrics.* and docs).
- Add unit and integration tests covering defrag correctness, spill/reload, and eviction decision boundaries. Add a perf canary script to validate latency under synthetic load.

Benchmarks: All numbers are from the perf-canary cluster (p4d tiles) using the long-context GPT-style model and a mixed load of 20% long (16k tokens) / 80% short requests.
- Baseline (main, before changes): median latency 48ms, p95 210ms, p99 1.4s, cache hit-rate 72%.
- With defrag + adaptive eviction (no spill): median 46ms (-4%), p95 190ms (-9.5%), p99 1.2s (-14%), cache hit-rate 78% (+6%).
- With spillover enabled (SSD-backed): median 47ms, p95 175ms (-16.5%), p99 850ms (-39%), effective memory pressure reduced by ~36% on average.

Compatibility & rollout: All features behind runtime flags. Default behavior on hosted remains enabled for defrag + adaptive eviction; spillover disabled by default and controlled via deployment config due to storage requirements. Documented config knobs and safe defaults in docs/kv-cache-ops.md.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for allocator and defragmentation logic
- [x] Integration test for spill/reload correctness across restarts
- [x] Perf canary and dashboards updated
- [x] Backwards-compatible: no changes to API surface
- [x] Feature-flag gating and operator docs

Related: previous KV work in pr-24690, pr-23847 and design notes ENG-1426.

Notes: A small flaky integration test (kv_spill_recovery.test) failed the first CI run due to a timing assumption; fixed by adding an explicit readiness probe to the spill store mock. The spill store uses a per-tenant namespace to avoid cross-tenant contamination and encrypts on-disk contents with the deployment KMS when enabled.

Requesting approval to merge after final perf canary completes in staging and SRE signoff on retention/IO budget for spill store.

review_comments:
Ethan Park: Can you clarify defrag worker scheduling? Is it CPU-bound or IO-bound and what is the safety threshold for not performing compaction under load?
Liang: Defrag runs at low priority and uses a cooperative throttling token bucket tied to request throughput. We skip compaction when request QPS > cfg.defrag.max_qps_threshold.

Sofia Martinez: Spill store persistence format—do we have versioning for forward compatibility?
Liang: Yes, spill blobs include a small header with version and tenant id. We added a migration path documented in docs/kv-cache-ops.md.

Priya Nair: Observability – add an eviction_decision tag to traces so we can filter policy outcomes in dashboards.
Liang: Added span attributes and a metric eviction_decision{action=compact|spill|evict}.

James O'Connor: What are failure modes if SSD writes fail (transient) — do we block inference?
Liang: We fall back to in-memory eviction path and emit a critical metric. We do not block requests; spill writes are best-effort and write failures degrade to eviction with a warn log.
Ethan Park (approving): Verified behavior on staging canary. Metrics look good; small nits in comments addressed. Approving.

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: background defragmentation, SSD-backed spillover for cold KV segments (optional), and an adaptive eviction policy that reduces tail latency and memory pressure. Feature flags available for staged rollout. See docs/kv-cache-ops.md for operator configuration and limits.
